answer.submission_route:
You can submit your appeal to TennCare Member Medical Appeals via several routes: 
1. Phone: Call toll-free at 1-800-878-3192 (they can file the appeal over the phone for you).
2. Online: Sign in to your account at TennCareConnect.TN.gov, click 'File a Medical Appeal', and follow the prompts. You can also use the TennCare Connect mobile app.
3. Mail: Send a completed TennCare Medical Appeal Form to: TennCare Member Medical Appeals, PO Box 593, Nashville, TN 37202-0593.
4. Fax: Fax the completed form to 1-888-345-5575.
answer.how_to_obtain_criteria: The clinical medical-necessity criteria are proprietary and licensed from McKesson (InterQual®). The patient can obtain a free copy of the specific criteria applied to their determination by calling TennCare Member Medical Appeals at 1-800-878-3192 or by calling the member services number on the back of their Medicaid ID card. Providers can also review a read-only version of the InterQual® criteria on the UnitedHealthcare Provider Portal at UHCprovider.com/policies > Clinical Guidelines > InterQual Clinical Criteria (requires portal registration/login).
answer.notes: Tennessee Medicaid (TennCare) delegates medical management and prior authorization reviews to Managed Care Organizations (MCOs) including UnitedHealthcare Community Plan of Tennessee. The governing policy for CPT 27447 in Tennessee is 'Surgery of the Knee (for Tennessee Only)' (Policy Number: CS068TN.AA, effective July 1, 2026), which formally adopts the InterQual® Clinical Planning (CP) guidelines for 'Total Joint Replacement (TJR), Knee'. Under these guidelines, patients are typically required to try and fail conservative treatment (such as a combination of NSAIDs/analgesics, physical therapy, and activity modifications) for at least 12 weeks before surgery is approved.

Decellularized Osteochondral Allograft Plugs (e.g., Chondrofix): A cylinder-shaped plug (graft) of healthy cartilage tissue and subchondral bone is taken from an area of the bone that does not carry weight (non-weight bearing). DeNovo Natural Tissue (NT) Graft: DeNovo NT consists of manually particulated cartilage obtained from juvenile allograft donor joints. The tissue fragments are mixed intraoperatively with fibrin glue before implantation in the prepared lesion (Farr et al., 2012).
